Package com.hottes.caleb.ultimateticktacktoe

Class BoardState

java.lang.Object
com.hottes.caleb.ultimateticktacktoe.gameindependant.GameState
com.hottes.caleb.ultimateticktacktoe.BoardState
public class BoardState extends GameState
Board state represents a state of an ultimate tick tac toe board. It is square and has a board size. so far only a board size of three has been used, but the code is hopefully able to support larger sizes too. this class contains various ways to create boards states and methods to manipulate them. There are getters and constructors for string hashes and bit sets. These are used to store board states in a memory efficient manner. The string hash method has been deprecated in favor of the bit set method.

    • getBitSet

      public BitSet getBitSet()
      format for the bitset data storage is as follows. the first 8 bits are a byte representing the board size. the next bit represents whose turn it is then each suboard is represented by 19 bits. they are indexed from the top left row first. so the top right is 2, and the bottom left is 6 for each of the sub boards the first bit of the 19 represents whether it is active or not. Then the next 9 bits represent if each of the cells contain anything. 0 if empty, 1 if either X or O the last 9 bits for each subboard represent whether each cell is occupied by player one (1) so 0 if the cell is 0 or -1 and 1 if the cell is 1
      Specified by:
      getBitSet in class GameState
      Returns:
      a bitset representing this board state

    • getValueNetworkInputVector

      public double[] getValueNetworkInputVector()
      used for machine learning returns a vector representing the state of this board. the player whose turn it is will be represented by the number 1 and the other player will be -1. so the board may be inverted. This method will also append on the end of the array a some 1's or -1's to represent which sub boards are active. So for each index 1 means active and -1 not. The reason why not 0 and 1 it for ML normalzation, i want to keep all the values between 1 and -1 and a boolean ought to be on the extremes takes aroung 2us to execute.
      Returns:
      a double[] of numbers representing the state of the board and which boards are active.
